questions.stem:
What are the significances of a practical approach to sugarcane production known as 'Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative'?
1. Seed cost is very low in this compared to the conventional method of cultivation.
2. Drip irrigation can be practiced very effectively in this.
3. There is no application of chemical/inorganic fertilizers at all in this.
4. The scope for intercropping is more in this compared to the conventional method of cultivation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**SSI = single-bud chip seedlings raised in a nursery, transplanted young at wide spacing (~5 ft).**

- **(1) True** — seed rate falls from ~6–8 t/ha of setts to ~1.5–2 t/ha of single buds, so seed cost drops sharply.
- **(2) True** — wide, regular row spacing is exactly what makes drip (and fertigation) practical.
- **(3) False** — SSI promotes organic matter and *balanced* nutrition; it never bans inorganic fertiliser. **Absolute words like "no application at all" are almost always the wrong statement.**
- **(4) True** — the wide inter-row gap in the first 60–90 days is deliberately used for intercrops.

Strike 3, keep 1, 2 and 4.
questions.tagging_note: Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative is a cultivation-practice question (seed rate, drip irrigation, intercropping) — sits in India-agriculture (GEO-17). No topic covers specific cultivation techniques/agronomy directly; ECO-14 added only for the input-subsidy/irrigation angle. Straddles GEO/ECO.

questions.stem: If a wetland of international importance is brought under the 'Montreux Record', what does it imply?
options: Changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring or are likely to occur in the wetland as a result of human interference
The country in which the wetland is located should enact a law to prohibit any human activity within five kilometres from the edge of the wetland
The survival of the wetland depends on the cultural practices and traditions of certain communities living in its vicinity and therefore the cultural diversity therein should not be destroyed
It is given the status of 'World Heritage Site'
questions.explanation_md:
**The Montreux Record is a register, kept under the Ramsar Convention, of listed wetlands where ecological character has changed, is changing, or is likely to change** due to technological development, pollution or other human interference.

- It is a **voluntary** listing — the Contracting Party must agree, and a site can be removed once remedial action works.
- India's Montreux Record sites: **Keoladeo (Bharatpur)** and **Loktak (Manipur)**. Chilika was on it and was removed in 2002 after restoration — a favourite UPSC hook.
- No buffer-zone law (b), no cultural criterion (c), and it has nothing to do with UNESCO World Heritage (d).

questions.stem: Which one of the following pairs of islands is separated from each other by the 'Ten Degree Channel'?
questions.explanation_md:
**The Ten Degree Channel separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar — i.e. the Andaman group from the Nicobar group** — lying along roughly 10°N.

Other channels worth fixing in memory:
- **Great Channel (Six Degree Channel)** — Great Nicobar and Sumatra (Indonesia).
- **Nine Degree Channel** — Minicoy and the rest of Lakshadweep.
- **Eight Degree Channel** — Minicoy and Maldives.
- **Sunda Strait** — Sumatra and Java.

questions.stem:
Consider the following pairs :

| *Programme/Project* | *Ministry* |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Drought-Prone Area Programme | Ministry of Agriculture |
| 2. Desert Development Programme | Ministry of Environment and Forests |
| 3. National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas | Ministry of Rural Development |

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation_md:
All three are cross-matched. **DPAP and DDP sit with the Ministry of Rural Development (Department of Land Resources); NWDPRA sits with the Ministry of Agriculture.**

- **(1) Wrong** — Drought Prone Areas Programme: Rural Development, not Agriculture.
- **(2) Wrong** — Desert Development Programme: Rural Development, not Environment & Forests.
- **(3) Wrong** — National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas: Agriculture (Dept. of Agriculture & Cooperation), not Rural Development.

Note: DPAP, DDP and IWDP were merged into the **Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP)** in 2009 under the Department of Land Resources, later folded into PMKSY–Watershed Development.
questions.tagging_note: Pure scheme-to-ministry mapping (DPAP, DDP, NWDPRA). The vocabulary has no topic for rural development / watershed & drought-management programmes — GEO-17 (irrigation, dryland agriculture) and CAI-10 (schemes tracker) are the nearest homes, neither is a real fit. Genuine gap in the syllabus tree. Format: three numbered pairs asking 'which ... is/are correctly matched', not a count, so tagged stmt_1_2_3 rather than pairs.

questions.stem:
With reference to Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), consider the following statements :
1. It is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Environment and Forests.
2. It strives to conserve nature through action-based research, education and public awareness.
3. It organizes and conducts nature trails and camps for the general public.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_md:
**BNHS is a non-governmental membership society founded in 1883 — not a government body.**

- **(1) Wrong** — it is an NGO/registered society. MoEF&CC funds some of its projects and DST recognises it as a Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation, but it is not an autonomous organisation *under* the ministry.
- **(2) Right** — its motto is "Conservation through research, education and public awareness."
- **(3) Right** — nature trails, camps and the *Hornbill* magazine are its best-known public activities.

BNHS did the vulture-decline (diclofenac) research and runs the Vulture Breeding Centres; its logo is the **Great Hornbill**.
questions.tagging_note: ENV-10 lists statutory/government bodies (NGT, CPCB, ZSI, BSI, WII); BNHS is a non-governmental society, so it is not named in the vocabulary but ENV-10 (environmental institutions) is the only sensible home.

questions.stem: With reference to 'Global Environment Facility', which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: It serves as financial mechanism for 'Convention on Biological Diversity' and 'United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change'
It undertakes scientific research on environmental issues at global level
It is an agency under OECD to facilitate the transfer of technology and funds to underdeveloped countries with specific aim to protect their environment
questions.explanation_md:
**GEF is a funding mechanism, not a research body.** Set up in 1991 around the Rio Earth Summit, it is an independent financial organisation whose secretariat is housed in the World Bank.

It serves as the financial mechanism for five conventions: **CBD, UNFCCC, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention (POPs) and Minamata Convention (mercury)**.

- (b) Wrong — it funds projects; it does not itself conduct global scientific research.
- (c) Wrong — it is **not** an OECD agency; membership is near-universal (180+ countries).

GEF also administers the LDCF and SCCF; the Green Climate Fund is a separate entity.
questions.tagging_note: GEF is the financial mechanism for both UNFCCC (ENV-13) and CBD (ENV-14); climate-finance angle makes ENV-13 the better primary.

questions.stem:
With reference to technologies for solar power production, consider the following statements :
1. 'Photovoltaics' is a technology that generates electricity by direct conversion of light into electricity, while 'Solar Thermal' is a technology that utilizes the Sun's rays to generate heat which is further used in electricity generation process.
2. Photovoltaics generates Alternating Current (AC), while Solar Thermal generates Direct Current (DC).
3. India has manufacturing base for Solar Thermal technology, but not for Photovoltaics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_md:
**Photovoltaic cells produce Direct Current, not AC — an inverter is needed before feeding the grid.**

- **(1) Right** — PV converts light straight to electricity by the photovoltaic effect; Solar Thermal (CSP) concentrates sunlight to raise steam that drives a turbine.
- **(2) Wrong** — PV output is DC; solar thermal drives a conventional turbine-generator, so its output is AC. The statement reverses both halves.
- **(3) Wrong** — the reverse is true: India has a substantial PV cell/module manufacturing base, while solar-thermal (CSP) manufacturing is negligible.

Only statement 1 stands.

questions.stem:
Consider the following languages :
1. Gujarati
2. Kannada
3. Telugu
Which of the above has/have been declared as 'Classical Language/Languages' by the Government?
questions.explanation_md:
**Gujarati has never been given classical-language status; Telugu and Kannada both got it in 2008.**

The position at the time of this paper: **Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014)**.

In October 2024 the Cabinet added **Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali**, taking the total to eleven — Gujarati is still not among them. Classical status brings international awards, a Centre of Excellence for Studies and UGC chairs; it is a Government of India decision, not a constitutional one.

questions.stem:
Consider the following pairs :
1. Dampa Tiger Reserve : Mizoram
2. Gumti Wildlife Sanctuary : Sikkim
3. Saramati Peak : Nagaland
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation_md:
**Gumti (Gomati) Wildlife Sanctuary is in Tripura, not Sikkim** — the only wrong pair.

- **(1) Right** — **Dampa** is Mizoram's only tiger reserve, near the Bangladesh border.
- **(2) Wrong** — Gumti WLS is in South Tripura; Tripura's others are Sepahijala, Trishna and Rowa. Sikkim's protected areas are Khangchendzonga NP, Fambong Lho, Barsey Rhododendron and Kyongnosla.
- **(3) Right** — **Saramati (~3,826 m) is Nagaland's highest peak**, in Kiphire district on the Myanmar border.

North-East tiger reserves to pair alongside: Namdapha and Pakke (Arunachal), Manas and Kaziranga (Assam), Buxa (West Bengal).
questions.tagging_note: Two of three pairs are protected areas (ENV-06); Saramati Peak is physiography/map work (GEO-12). Format: 'which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched' is a which-not-how-many question, so stmt_1_2_3 rather than pairs.

questions.stem:
With reference to a conservation organization called 'Wetlands International', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is an intergovernmental organization formed by the countries which are signatories to Ramsar Convention.
2. It works at the field level to develop and mobilize knowledge, and use the practical experience to advocate for better policies.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**Wetlands International is a global non-profit NGO headquartered in Ede, the Netherlands — not an intergovernmental body.**

- **(1) Wrong** — it was not created by Ramsar signatories and has no treaty basis; it grew out of IWRB/AWB/Wetlands for the Americas, merged in 1995. It *is* an official International Organisation Partner of Ramsar (with IUCN, BirdLife, WWF, WWT) and runs the **International Waterbird Census** and the Ramsar Sites Information Service — partnership, not membership.
- **(2) Right** — its stated method is exactly field-level work to build and mobilise knowledge, then use that practical experience to advocate better policy.

The intergovernmental-vs-NGO distinction is the whole question.
questions.tagging_note: Wetlands International is an international conservation NGO. ENV-10 covers only Indian institutions, so the question lands on the Ramsar/conventions topic (ENV-14) plus wetland ecosystems (ENV-04). International conservation organisations (IUCN, WWF, Wetlands International) are not explicitly covered anywhere in the tree — a recurring gap, given Q5 and Q6 hit the same edge.
questions.transcription_note: The scan prints the lead-in as 'Select the corr.ct answer' — a broken glyph in the print, read as 'correct'. Confirmed on the English page (PDF p.6) and against the Hindi mirror on p-07.

questions.stem:
With reference to a grouping of countries known as BRICS, consider the following statements :
1. The First Summit of BRICS was held in Rio de Janeiro in 2009.
2. South Africa was the last to join the BRICS grouping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_md:
**Statement 1 — wrong.** The first BRIC summit was held at **Yekaterinburg, Russia (16 June 2009)**, not Rio de Janeiro. The 2nd was Brasília 2010, the 3rd Sanya (China) 2011 — the first with South Africa.

**Statement 2 — correct.** BRIC became BRICS when **South Africa was invited in Dec 2010 and attended from the Sanya summit (2011)** — the last member for the entire period the question covers. (Only in 2024 did Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE join.)

So **2 only → (b)**.

questions.stem:
Consider the following diseases :
1. Diphtheria
2. Chickenpox
3. Smallpox
Which of the above diseases has/have been eradicated in India?
questions.explanation_md:
**1. Diphtheria — not eradicated.** Still occurs in India; it is a vaccine-preventable disease under UIP (DPT), with outbreaks reported regularly.

**2. Chickenpox (varicella) — not eradicated.** Common in India; the vaccine is not even in the routine national schedule.

**3. Smallpox — eradicated.** India's **last case was in May 1975 (Bihar); India declared smallpox-free in 1977, world declared free by WHO in 1980**. Smallpox is the only human disease ever eradicated.

So **3 only → (b)**. (Guinea worm and polio were eliminated from India in 2000 and 2014, but neither is in the list.)
questions.tagging_note: Disease eradication (smallpox) sits squarely in SNT-02; SNT-04 added only because eradication in India ran through national health missions.

questions.stem:
Which of the following phenomena might have influenced the evolution of organisms?
1. Continental drift
2. Glacial cycles
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**1. Continental drift — yes.** Splitting Pangaea/Gondwana separated populations, causing geographic isolation and allopatric speciation — the classic case is India's isolation as it drifted north, and the marsupials of Australia and South America.

**2. Glacial cycles — yes.** Ice ages repeatedly fragmented habitats into refugia, shifted sea levels (opening/closing land bridges like Beringia) and applied strong cold selection — a major driver of speciation and extinction, including in human evolution.

**Both are standard drivers of evolution — anything that isolates populations or changes selection pressure influences it. → (c)**
questions.tagging_note: GAP: no topic in the vocabulary covers evolution, natural selection or speciation. SNT-01 is 'cell, genetics, human systems, nutrition' — genetics is the nearest hook but evolutionary biology is not named anywhere. GEO-03 supplies continental drift and ENV-05 the biodiversity/speciation angle, so the question is only covered by triangulation. Worth adding an evolution sub-topic under SNT-01.

questions.stem:
Other than poaching, what are the possible reasons for the decline in the population of Ganges River Dolphins?
1. Construction of dams and barrages on rivers
2. Increase in the population of crocodiles in rivers
3. Getting trapped in fishing nets accidentally
4. Use of synthetic fertilizers and other agricultural chemicals in crop-fields in the vicinity of rivers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
The Ganges River Dolphin (*Platanista gangetica*, National Aquatic Animal, Schedule I, IUCN Endangered) is blind and hunts by echolocation.

**1. Dams/barrages — yes.** Farakka and other barrages fragment the population, block migration and cut dry-season flow. Main threat.

**2. Crocodiles — no.** Gharial and mugger populations are themselves declining, and they are not significant dolphin predators. This is the odd statement out.

**3. Fishing nets — yes.** Accidental **bycatch entanglement in gillnets is a leading cause of mortality**.

**4. Agrochemicals — yes.** Pesticide/fertiliser runoff biomagnifies in this top predator and causes toxic loads plus eutrophication.

**1, 3 and 4 only → (c).** Eliminating statement 2 alone settles the question.
questions.tagging_note: ENV-08 names the Gangetic Dolphin project explicitly; ENV-11 carries the agro-chemical pollution strand in statement 4.

questions.stem: The Radcliffe Committee was appointed to
options: solve the problem of minorities in India
give effect to the Independence Bill
delimit the boundaries between India and Pakistan
enquire into the riots in East Bengal
questions.explanation_md:
**Sir Cyril Radcliffe** chaired the **Boundary Commissions for Punjab and Bengal (1947)** — his job was to **draw the partition line between India and Pakistan**, published on 17 August 1947, two days after independence. He had never visited India and finished in about five weeks.

- (a) minorities — that was the Cabinet Mission / earlier constitutional discussions.
- (b) giving effect to the Independence Bill — that was Mountbatten's administrative machinery, not Radcliffe.
- (d) East Bengal riots — Radcliffe had no enquiry role.

**→ (c)**

questions.stem:
Brominated flame retardants are used in many household products like mattresses and upholstery. Why is there some concern about their use?
1. They are highly resistant to degradation in the environment.
2. They are able to accumulate in humans and animals.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
Brominated flame retardants (PBDEs, HBCD, etc.) are added to foam, mattresses, upholstery and electronics casings.

**1. Correct — persistent.** They resist degradation and are classed as **Persistent Organic Pollutants; HBCD and some PBDEs are listed under the Stockholm Convention**.

**2. Correct — bioaccumulative.** Being lipophilic, they accumulate in fatty tissue and biomagnify up the food chain; they are detected in human blood, breast milk and in Arctic wildlife far from any source. Endocrine-disruption and neurodevelopmental concerns follow from this.

**Both → (c).** Rule of thumb: persistence + bioaccumulation + toxicity is exactly why a chemical becomes a POP.
questions.tagging_note: Persistence and bioaccumulation are the POPs criteria, so ENV-14 (Stockholm Convention) is the genuine second topic alongside pollution.

questions.stem:
Consider the following :
1. Bats
2. Bears
3. Rodents
The phenomenon of hibernation can be observed in which of the above kinds of animals?
options: Hibernation cannot be observed in any of the above
questions.explanation_md:
**1. Bats — yes.** Temperate bats are textbook hibernators, dropping body temperature and metabolism for months in caves.

**2. Bears — yes (as UPSC treats it).** Bears undergo winter dormancy/denning; zoologists call it torpor rather than true hibernation because body temperature falls only modestly and they can rouse, but in the exam's usage bears hibernate.

**3. Rodents — yes.** Ground squirrels, marmots, dormice and hamsters are among the deepest hibernators known.

**All three → (c).** Even a purist reading gives at least bats and rodents, and no option offers "1 and 3 only", so (c) is forced.
questions.tagging_note: GAP: hibernation is general animal physiology/zoology, which no topic covers. SNT-01 is limited to cell, genetics, human systems and nutrition; ENV-07 is Indian flora and fauna, and this question is about bats/bears/rodents generally, not Indian species. Neither is a true fit.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the largest Committee of the Parliament?
questions.explanation_md:
Membership of the financial/other standing committees:

- **Estimates Committee — 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha** (no Rajya Sabha representation). **Largest.**
- Public Accounts Committee — 22 (15 LS + 7 RS).
- Committee on Public Undertakings — 22 (15 LS + 7 RS).
- Committee on Petitions — 15 (Lok Sabha) / 10 (Rajya Sabha).

All are elected annually by proportional representation through single transferable vote; a minister cannot be a member, and the PAC chair is by convention from the Opposition.

**→ (b)**

questions.stem:
Which of the following adds/add carbon dioxide to the carbon cycle on the planet Earth?
1. Volcanic action
2. Respiration
3. Photosynthesis
4. Decay of organic matter
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**1. Volcanic action — adds.** Volcanoes and metamorphic degassing release CO₂ from the lithosphere into the atmosphere.

**2. Respiration — adds.** Plants and animals oxidise organic carbon and exhale CO₂.

**3. Photosynthesis — removes.** **This is the one sink in the list** — it fixes atmospheric CO₂ into carbohydrates.

**4. Decay of organic matter — adds.** Decomposers respire and return carbon as CO₂ (or CH₄ in anaerobic conditions).

**1, 2 and 4 only → (c).** Spotting photosynthesis as the sink is the whole question.

questions.stem:
If you walk through countryside, you are likely to see some birds stalking alongside the cattle to seize the insects disturbed by their movement through grasses. Which of the following is/are such bird/birds?
1. Painted Stork
2. Common Myna
3. Black-necked Crane
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
The behaviour described is **commensal foraging** — walking with grazing cattle to snap up insects flushed from the grass. Classically the Cattle Egret, and among the options only one bird does it.

**1. Painted Stork — no.** A wetland wader; it feeds by tactile fishing with its bill submerged in shallow water, not by following cattle in grassland.

**2. Common Myna — yes.** A ground-foraging bird of open country that routinely walks beside grazing cattle (and even perches on them) taking disturbed insects.

**3. Black-necked Crane — no.** A **high-altitude bird of Ladakh and the Tibetan plateau** (Tsokar/Tsomoriri), feeding on roots, tubers and invertebrates in marshes — not a countryside cattle-follower.

**2 only → (b)**
questions.tagging_note: Bird identification question. ENV-07 (Indian flora and fauna) is the only home for species-recognition items, though it is framed around endemic and flagship species rather than common birds and their feeding behaviour.

questions.stem: In medieval India, the designations 'Mahattara' and 'Pattakila' were used for
questions.explanation_md:
**Both are village-level officials in medieval land-grant inscriptions.** *Mahattara* (from Sanskrit *mahattara*, "the greater one") = the village elder/headman; *Pattakila* is the Sanskritised form that becomes **Patel / Patil** in Gujarat and Maharashtra — the hereditary village headman who collected revenue and settled disputes.

Neither term is military (that would be *senapati*, *dandanayaka*), priestly (*shrotriya*, *ritvij*), or guild-related (*shreshthin*, *jyeshthaka* head the *shreni*).
questions.tagging_note: 'Mahattara' and 'Pattakila' are village-headman designations from early medieval land-grant charters (c. 8th-12th c.), so ANM-10 (early medieval) is the closest bucket, with ANM-08 (Gupta/post-Gupta) as the adjacent period. The tree has no dedicated topic for early medieval village administration and local officials — that vocabulary sits between ANM-08, ANM-10 and ANM-11.

questions.stem: Lichens, which are capable of initiating ecological succession even on a bare rock, are actually a symbiotic association of
questions.explanation_md:
**A lichen is a fungus + a photosynthetic partner (usually a green alga).** The fungus (mycobiont) supplies structure, water and mineral absorption; the alga (phycobiont) supplies food by photosynthesis.

Why they are pioneers: the fungal hyphae secrete organic acids that chemically weather bare rock into the first thin soil, letting mosses and then herbs follow — classic **xerarch (lithosere) succession**.

Caveat worth knowing: in some lichens the photobiont is a *cyanobacterium* (e.g. *Nostoc*), but the standard textbook answer is algae + fungi.

questions.stem:
If you travel through the Himalayas, you are likely to see which of the following plants naturally growing there?
1. Oak
2. Rhododendron
3. Sandalwood
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
1. **Oak (*Quercus*) — yes.** Dominant in Himalayan moist/dry temperate forests, roughly 1,200–3,500 m (banj oak, kharsu).
2. **Rhododendron — yes.** Temperate to alpine Himalaya; *R. arboreum* (buransh) is Uttarakhand's state tree, and Sikkim/Arunachal have dozens of species.
3. **Sandalwood (*Santalum album*) — no.** It is a **tropical dry deciduous / scrub species of the peninsular Deccan** — Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, southern Andhra. It is a root hemi-parasite needing hot, dry, frost-free conditions; it does not grow naturally in the Himalayas.

So **1 and 2 only**.
questions.tagging_note: Straddles GEO (India's forest types by altitude — temperate oak/rhododendron vs tropical sandalwood) and ENV-07 (Indian flora).

questions.stem:
Which of the following are some important pollutants released by steel industry in India?
1. Oxides of sulphur
2. Oxides of nitrogen
3. Carbon monoxide
4. Carbon dioxide
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
An integrated steel plant burns coal/coke at every stage, so it emits **all four**.

- **SO₂** — sulphur in coal and coke, plus sinter plant and coke ovens.
- **NOₓ** — any high-temperature combustion fixes atmospheric nitrogen.
- **CO** — iron ore is *reduced* by carbon monoxide in the blast furnace; blast-furnace gas and coke-oven gas are CO-rich, and incomplete combustion adds more.
- **CO₂** — the end product of all that carbon; steel is one of the most CO₂-intensive industries.

Also emitted (not asked): particulate matter/fly ash and fluorides.

Rule of thumb for such questions: **when every listed pollutant is a normal product of coal combustion, take "all of the above".**

questions.stem:
Which of the following Kingdoms were associated with the life of the Buddha?
1. Avanti
2. Gandhara
3. Kosala
4. Magadha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
The Buddha's life was spent almost entirely in the **middle Gangetic plain**.

1. **Avanti (Ujjain) — no.** The Buddha never travelled there; his disciple Mahakatyayana preached there, and Pradyota was a contemporary king, but Avanti is not part of *his life*.
2. **Gandhara (Taxila) — no.** Far north-west; outside his wanderings entirely.
3. **Kosala — yes.** Kapilavastu/Lumbini lay under Kosala's overlordship; he spent the largest number of rain-retreats at **Shravasti (Jetavana)**; Prasenajit was his patron.
4. **Magadha — yes.** Enlightenment at **Bodh Gaya**, first monastery at Rajagriha (Venuvana), patrons **Bimbisara and Ajatashatru**.

So **3 and 4 only**. Note the option wording: only option (c) carries "only", which fits a two-item answer.

(The other two janapadas of his world worth remembering: **Vajji/Vaishali** and **Kashi**.)
questions.tagging_note: Tests the political geography of the Mahajanapadas (Kosala, Magadha, Avanti, Gandhara) as it maps onto the Buddha's life, so it sits across ANM-03 and ANM-04.

questions.stem: प्रत्येक वर्ष कतिपय विशिष्ट समुदाय/जनजाति, पारिस्थितिक रूप से महत्त्वपूर्ण, मास-भर चलने वाले अभियान/त्यौहार के दौरान फलदार वृक्षों की पौध का रोपण करते हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से ऐसे समुदाय/जनजाति हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
**Gond and Korku** — tribes of the **Satpura–Melghat belt of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra** — plant fruit-tree saplings during their month-long annual festival, an ecologically significant custom UPSC picked up from Environment Ministry material.

Eliminate the rest by geography/livelihood:
- **Bhutia and Lepcha** — Sikkim/Darjeeling, associated with the Khangchendzonga landscape, not a tree-planting festival.
- **Irula and Toda** — Nilgiris; Todas are pastoralists (buffalo, sacred dairies), Irulas famous for snake-catching.
- **Sahariya (MP/Rajasthan, a PVTG) and Agariya (iron-smelting/salt-making)** — no such festival.

1. व्यापार सन्तुलन
2. विदेशी परिसम्पत्तियाँ
3. अदृश्यों का सन्तुलन
4. विशेष आहरण अधिकार
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
**Current account = balance of trade (visibles) + balance of invisibles.**

1. **Balance of trade — yes.** Merchandise exports minus imports.
2. **Foreign assets — no.** Acquisition of assets abroad is a **capital account** item.
3. **Balance of invisibles — yes.** Services (software, travel), income (interest, dividends) and **unilateral transfers (remittances)** — India's invisibles surplus is what keeps the CAD manageable despite a large trade deficit.
4. **SDRs — no.** Special Drawing Rights are an IMF reserve asset — **capital account / reserves**, not current.

So **1 and 3**. One-line test: *if it is an income or expenditure flow it is current; if it changes ownership of assets/liabilities it is capital.*

questions.explanation_md:
Both terms are **RBI banking/monetary-policy vocabulary**.

- **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)** — window opened by RBI in May 2011 letting scheduled commercial banks borrow overnight against SLR securities (dipping below SLR up to a permitted limit). MSF rate sits **above the repo rate** and forms the upper bound of the LAF corridor.
- **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** — the deposit base on which **CRR and SLR are computed**. Demand liabilities = current/savings, demand drafts, overdue deposits; time liabilities = fixed deposits, staff security deposits, time portion of savings; "net" = after deducting inter-bank assets.

Nothing to do with telecom, warfare or agriculture. Answer (a).

questions.explanation_md:
**Business Correspondents (Bank Mitra)** were introduced by RBI in 2006 to extend banking to unbanked/branchless areas. They are retail agents with a micro-ATM/handheld device linked to the bank's core banking system.

**Statement 1 — correct.** BCs are the delivery arm for **DBT**: MGNREGA wages, old-age/widow pensions, scholarships and other social-security payments are paid out in the village itself, removing the trip to a distant branch.

**Statement 2 — correct.** BCs are explicitly permitted to accept **small-value deposits and pay out cash withdrawals** (plus receipt/delivery of remittances, recovery of principal/interest, sale of micro-insurance and pension products), all with biometric authentication.

Both true. Answer (c).

questions.stem:
भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था के सन्दर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/से 'सांविधिक आरक्षित आवश्यकताओं' का/के उद्देश्य है/हैं?
1. केन्द्रीय बैंक को, बैंकों द्वारा निर्मित की जा सकने वाली अग्रिम राशियों पर नियंत्रण रखने की सक्षमता प्रदान करना
2. बैंकों में जनता की जमा राशियों को सुरक्षित व तरल रखना
3. व्यावसायिक बैंकों को अत्यधिक लाभ कमाने से रोकना
4. बैंकों को दिन-प्रतिदिन की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए पर्याप्त कोष्ठ नकदी (वॉल्ट कैश) रखने को बाध्य करना
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
"सांविधिक आरक्षित आवश्यकताएँ" = CRR (RBI अधिनियम, धारा 42) + SLR (बैंककारी विनियमन अधिनियम, धारा 24). The question asks for the **उद्देश्य** — the purpose the instrument was created to serve — not for every pleasant side effect it happens to produce. Test each statement against that.

- **1 — correct.** Reserve requirements lock away a slice of NDTL, which caps the money multiplier and therefore the volume of advances the banking system can create out of a given deposit base. This is the textbook definition of the instrument, and the reason it sits in the monetary-policy toolkit alongside the repo rate.
- **2 — wrong, and this single statement is the whole question.** It claims the objective is to keep *the public's deposits* "सुरक्षित व तरल". Depositor **safety** is delivered by a completely different set of instruments — capital adequacy (CRAR/Basel norms), provisioning and NPA rules, RBI supervision, and DICGC insurance (₹1 lakh per depositor in 2014). A bank can be fully CRR- and SLR-compliant on the day it fails, and its depositors still lose. Nor do these reserves supply **liquidity** to depositors: CRR balances sit with the RBI, non-lendable and (since 2007) non-interest-bearing, and SLR assets are encumbered — falling below the floor attracts penal interest, so it is precisely the money a bank may *not* draw on. A statutory floor a bank is punished for touching cannot be a buffer for paying depositors.
- **3 — wrong.** No reserve requirement anywhere is imposed to cap bank profits. Reserve ratios do compress the interest margin, but that is a cost of the instrument, not its उद्देश्य. Bank profitability in India is left to competition and deregulated interest rates, not to Section 42.
- **4 — wrong.** CRR must be maintained as an average fortnightly **balance with the RBI**, not as vault cash; vault cash is not eligible for CRR in India. And a flat statutory percentage of total liabilities cannot possibly be an instrument for day-to-day till requirements, which vary by branch, season and festival and are managed by the bank's own treasury. (SLR may include cash in hand, which is the near-miss that makes this statement tempting — but even there the ratio is set for monetary control and captive government borrowing, never calibrated to a branch's daily cash needs.)

Only 1 survives — **(a)**.

**The trap, and why "1 और 2" fails.** Older banking texts do say SLR "ensures the solvency/liquidity of banks", and a candidate carrying that line straight into statement 2 lands on (b). But the statement does not say *solvency of banks*; it says the objective is to keep **जनता की जमा राशियों** safe and liquid — a compound claim about depositors, and both halves belong to other instruments. The decisive evidence is historical: between 1991 and 2014 the RBI cut CRR from 15% to 4% and SLR from 38.5% to 22% while deposits multiplied several times over. If depositor safety and liquidity were the purpose of these ratios, those cuts would have been an outright scandal. They were uncontroversial because the purpose is **monetary control** — and depositor protection was strengthened over the same years through an entirely separate channel: capital norms and deposit insurance. (Basel III's LCR, phased in from 2015, exists as the actual liquidity standard precisely because SLR was never one.)

Note also how UPSC built the options — `{1}`, `{1,2}`, `{2,3}`, `{1,2,3,4}`. Once 3 is dismissed as absurd, the whole question is a single yes/no on statement 2. When a "which of these is an objective" question is engineered to hinge on one statement, that statement almost always describes a **by-product of the instrument, or another instrument's job**. Here it is both.

**Durable:** sort banking regulations by the problem they were built to solve — CRR/SLR = monetary control (how much credit the system may create); CRAR + provisioning + PCA = solvency; DICGC = depositor compensation; LCR/NSFR = liquidity. Statements that shuffle a tool from one column into another are UPSC's standard distractor in this topic.

**Agni-IV** (DRDO, first successful test Nov 2011).

**3 — wrong on range.** Agni-IV carries roughly a **1-tonne warhead to about 3,500–4,000 km**. 7,500 km is **Agni-V/ICBM class** (Agni-V ≈ 5,000+ km). The number is the giveaway.

2. भारत में कोयला-संस्तर मैथेन स्रोत बहुतायत में हैं, किन्तु अब तक शेल गैस के स्रोत नहीं पाए गए हैं।

questions.explanation_md:
**Statement 1 — wrong.** CBM is indeed largely **methane adsorbed on coal seams**, but **shale gas is also predominantly methane** trapped in fine-grained sedimentary (shale) rock, released by hydraulic fracturing. Calling shale gas "only a mixture of propane and butane" is false.

**Statement 2 — wrong.** India has both. CBM basins: Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, Sohagpur. **Shale gas resources have been identified** in the **Cambay, Krishna–Godavari, Cauvery, Assam–Arakan, Damodar and Indo-Gangetic** basins; India's shale gas policy came in 2013 and **ONGC drilled the first shale gas well at Icchapur, North 24 Parganas (West Bengal) in 2011**.

Neither statement holds. Answer (d).

questions.explanation_md:
**Changpa** (Champa) — nomadic pastoralists of the **Changthang plateau in eastern Ladakh** (then J&K, now UT of Ladakh), of Tibetan stock; a related group lives in Tibet.

**1 — wrong.** Not Uttarakhand. They are **Ladakh/Changthang**, at ~4,000+ m altitude around Tso Moriri and Hanle.

**2 — correct.** They rear the **Changthangi (Pashmina) goat**, source of the ultra-fine **pashm** used for Kashmiri pashmina shawls — they also keep yak and sheep.

**3 — correct.** The Changpa are a **notified Scheduled Tribe** in the erstwhile J&K list.

Only 2 and 3. Answer (b).

questions.stem:
भारत में मृदा अपक्षय समस्या निम्नलिखित में से किससे/किनसे सम्बन्धित है/हैं?
1. वेदिका कृषि
2. वनोन्मूलन
3. उष्णकटिबन्धी जलवायु
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
**Answer: (b) — only 2.**

The whole question turns on one term in statement 1: **वेदिका कृषि = terrace cultivation**, not शिफ्टिंग/झूम कृषि (shifting cultivation). Those two get mixed up constantly, and only one of them is a cause of soil loss.

**Statement 1 — वेदिका कृषि (terrace cultivation): not a cause. It is the cure.**
Terracing cuts a long slope into short level steps. That shortens slope length, drops runoff velocity, and lets water infiltrate instead of sheet-washing the topsoil away. NCERT (Class X, *Contemporary India II*, Ch. 1) lists it in the **soil conservation** paragraph alongside contour ploughing, strip cropping and shelter belts — the same list UPSC habitually draws these statements from. Terracing is what the Nilgiris, the Himalayan foothills and Uttarakhand hillsides use *because* of the erosion problem, not what creates it.

What the solver was probably thinking of is **झूम / स्थानान्तरी कृषि (shifting cultivation)**, which genuinely is a standard cause — slash, burn, crop for two seasons, abandon bare slope to the monsoon. Swap that word into statement 1 and the answer really would be (d). UPSC did not put that word there.

**Statement 2 — वनोन्मूलन (deforestation): the textbook cause.** Remove the root mat and the canopy, and raindrop impact plus unimpeded runoff strips the A-horizon. This is the first item on every standard list of causes for India — Shiwaliks, Chambal ravines, the northeastern hills.

**Statement 3 — उष्णकटिबन्धीय जलवायु (tropical climate): a background condition, not the problem's cause.** The whole of peninsular India sits in it, yet erosion rates vary from negligible to catastrophic across that same climate. The variable that changes is **ground cover**, not the thermal regime: an undisturbed tropical rainforest has among the *lowest* erosion rates on earth. Climate supplies the energy; land use decides whether that energy hits bare soil. Note too that the erosion literature's term of art is **rainfall erosivity / monsoon intensity**, which is not the same thing as "tropical climate" — the paper gave the loose category, not the operative factor.

(If you read मृदा **अपक्षय** as *weathering* rather than soil loss, tropical climate would obviously belong — deep lateritic weathering profiles are a tropical signature. But the stem calls it a **समस्या**, a problem. Weathering is soil *formation*; the problem being asked about is soil *degradation*.)

**Why (d) cannot be salvaged — the option structure decides it.**
The four options are 1&2, 2 only, 1&3, 1,2,3. There is **no "2 and 3 only"**. So the moment statement 1 is out — and a conservation technique cannot be a cause of the thing it conserves against — options (a), (c) and (d) all fall together, and (b) is the only survivor. You never even have to settle the argument about statement 3. That is the exam-hall shortcut: identify वेदिका कृषि correctly and the question is finished in ten seconds.

**Carry forward:** on cause-of-erosion statements, sort every item into *causes* (deforestation, overgrazing, shifting cultivation, ploughing down-slope, mining, construction) or *cures* (terracing, contour bunding, strip cropping, shelter belts, afforestation). Climate almost never appears on the causes list in NCERT-sourced questions.

questions.explanation_md:
**Seasonal reversal of winds is the defining feature of the monsoon climate.** The word *mausim* itself means season.

- Summer: intense land heating over Asia creates low pressure; winds blow **sea → land (SW monsoon)**, wet.
- Winter: land cools, high pressure builds; winds blow **land → sea (NE monsoon)**, dry.

Why not the others:
- **Equatorial climate** — calm, converging trade winds in the ITCZ, no seasonal reversal; rain all year.
- **Mediterranean climate** — wet winter (westerlies), dry summer (offshore trades). Rainfall shifts seasonally, but the wind belts *migrate*; they do not reverse direction by 180°.

Answer **(c)**.

Examples: the **Dashavatara temple at Deogarh**, and the Brahmeshvara/Kandariya Mahadeva group at Khajuraho.

Don't be misled by *panch* into picking "assembly of village elders" (that is the panchayat) — the suffix **-ayatana means "shrine/abode"**. Answer **(c)**.

questions.explanation_md:
The question demands conservation of **biodiversity *and* traditional human life together** — only one option allows people to live inside.

**Biosphere Reserves** use a three-zone design: a strictly protected **core**, a **buffer** for research and limited use, and a **transition/manipulation zone where local communities live, farm and practise traditional livelihoods**. Conserving human cultural life is an explicit UNESCO MAB objective.

Why not:
- **National Park** — strictest; no human rights or grazing permitted.
- **Wildlife Sanctuary** — some regulated rights, but the focus is fauna, not culture.
- **Botanical Garden** — ex-situ collection of plants; no communities at all.

Answer **(a)**.

Statement-wise:

1. **Correct** — beyond about 3 °C the terrestrial biosphere flips from a net carbon *sink* to a net carbon **source** (soil respiration and forest dieback, e.g. Amazon, outpace CO₂ fertilisation). This is a standard IPCC "reasons for concern" finding.

4. **Wrong** — cereal yields fall sharply in the tropics, but cultivation actually expands poleward; "nowhere in the world" is absurd.

**Reject options with the absolute words "all" and "nowhere"** — 1 and 2 only.

1. मृदा के बह जाने की रोकथाम
2. देश की बारहमासी नदियों को मौसमी नदियों से जोड़ना
3. वर्षा-जल संग्रहण तथा भौम-जलस्तर का पुनर्भरण
4. प्राकृतिक वनस्पतियों का पुनर्जनन
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
Statement-wise on the **Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP, 2009; later folded into PMKSY–Watershed Development)**:

1. **Correct** — checking soil erosion/run-off through bunding, contour trenching and gully plugging is a core objective.
2. **Wrong** — **linking rivers is the National River Linking Project (NPP of the NWDA), not a watershed programme**; watershed work is local, ridge-to-valley, within a micro-catchment. And the phrasing itself is nonsense.
3. **Correct** — rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge via check dams, percolation tanks and farm ponds.
4. **Correct** — regeneration of natural vegetation/afforestation on degraded watershed land.

So 1, 3 and 4.
questions.tagging_note: Straddles Geography, Environment and schemes. Soil erosion prevention and vegetation regeneration are soil-degradation content (GEO-15); rainwater harvesting/groundwater recharge is irrigation-side agriculture (GEO-17); IWDP itself is a government programme (CAI-10). No dedicated watershed-management or water-resources topic exists in the vocabulary — that is a genuine gap, since water resources is a recurring Prelims theme.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi-language page; transcribed verbatim in Hindi. English text is on the facing even page, not extracted.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से भारत में 'योजना' से सम्बद्ध हैं?
1. वित्त आयोग
2. राष्ट्रीय विकास परिषद्
3. संघीय ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय
4. संघीय शहरी विकास मंत्रालय
5. संसद
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
**Official answer: (c) — केवल 2 और 5**

The whole question turns on one term of art: **"योजना" / "Planning"** in the Indian fiscal system is not a loose synonym for "spending money on schemes". It names a specific institutional chain — **Plan formulation → NDC approval → Parliament's sanction**. Indian public finance drew a formal line between **Plan** and **non-Plan**, and the question is testing exactly that line.

**Why 2 and 5 are in**

- **राष्ट्रीय विकास परिषद् (NDC)** — chaired by the PM, with all CMs and Union ministers. It is the apex body that *reviews and approves* the Five Year Plan before it is finalised. Its only job is the plan. Nothing is more squarely "associated with Planning".
- **संसद (Parliament)** — the Five Year Plan document is laid before and approved by Parliament, and every rupee of plan outlay reaches a ministry only through the annual budget's demands for grants. Without Parliament the plan has no money and no force.

**Why 1 fails — this is the discriminator**

The **वित्त आयोग (Finance Commission)** is a constitutional body under **Article 280** with a mandate that is the *mirror image* of planning: distribution of tax proceeds between the Centre and States, and **grants-in-aid of revenues** to cover States' **non-Plan revenue gap**. Plan assistance to States was never its business — that flowed from the Planning Commission through the **Gadgil–Mukherjee formula**, cleared by the NDC. The Finance Commission was, by design and by decades of practice, the **non-Plan** authority. A candidate who knows the Plan / non-Plan division rules out 1 immediately.

That single elimination decides the question: options (a), (b) and (d) all contain 1, so only **(c)** can stand.

**Why 3 and 4 fail**

The **ग्रामीण विकास** and **शहरी विकास** ministries are **executing / implementing** agencies. They run schemes (MGNREGA, PMAY and the rest) that were framed under the Plan — but so does every other Union ministry. Implementing a plan is not being part of the planning machinery. Notice the structural clue in the stem: the list names **only two** ministries out of dozens. If "spends plan money" counted as association with planning, the selection would be arbitrary and the statement meaningless — the setter would have had to include Health, Agriculture, Education and every other ministry. The fact that exactly two implementing ministries are offered is the trap, not the answer.

**Why (d) is tempting and why it loses**

(d) comes from reading **"सम्बद्ध हैं" / "associated with"** at its loosest: anything that touches development money is "associated". Under that reading everything in the list qualifies — which is precisely why it cannot be the intended reading, since it makes the question unanswerable as a discrimination test. UPSC is using "planning" in its precise Indian-polity sense: the bodies whose **institutional function is the plan itself** (NDC formulating and approving it, Parliament sanctioning it), not the body that handles the **non-Plan** side (Finance Commission) and not the ministries that merely **spend** what the plan allots.

**Takeaway for revision:** whenever "योजना / Planning" appears with the Finance Commission in the same list, recall the **Plan vs non-Plan** divide — Finance Commission = non-Plan revenue gap (Art. 280); Planning Commission + NDC = Plan; Parliament = final approval. That one line settles most questions of this family.
questions.tagging_note: Subject straddle: the spine is India's planning machinery (NDC, Planning Commission/NITI, Parliament) = ECO-19, but the Finance Commission option is Polity constitutional-bodies content = POL-24.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/से मंत्रिमण्डल सचिवालय का/के कार्य है/हैं?
1. मंत्रिमण्डल बैठकों के लिए कार्यसूची तैयार करना
2. मंत्रिमण्डल समितियों के लिए सचिवालयी सहायता
3. मंत्रालयों को वित्तीय संसाधनों का आबंटन
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
Statement-wise on the **Cabinet Secretariat** (under the direct charge of the PM, headed by the Cabinet Secretary):

1. **Correct** — it prepares the agenda for Cabinet meetings, circulates papers, and records and circulates the decisions.
2. **Correct** — it provides secretarial assistance to Cabinet Committees, and keeps the Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules and (Allocation of Business) Rules.
3. **Wrong** — **allocation of financial resources to ministries is done by the Ministry of Finance through the Budget** (Department of Expenditure / Department of Economic Affairs), never by the Cabinet Secretariat.

So 1 and 2 only. The Cabinet Secretariat coordinates and records; it does not hold the purse.
questions.tagging_note: Cabinet Secretariat has no topic of its own; POL-19 (Laxmikanth Ch.23,24 — Cabinet Committees) is the nearest home since it covers secretarial support to Cabinet committees, with POL-17 for the Council of Ministers context. Statement 3 (allocation of financial resources) is really a Finance Ministry/budget distractor.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
संवैधानिक सरकार वह है
1. जो राज्य की सत्ता के हित में व्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता पर प्रभावकारी प्रतिबन्ध लगाती है
2. जो व्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता के हित में राज्य की सत्ता पर प्रभावकारी प्रतिबन्ध लगाती है
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
**Constitutionalism means limited government: effective restraints on the power of the State in the interest of individual liberty** — exactly statement 2.

Statement 1 inverts this. A government that curbs individual liberty in the interest of state authority is authoritarian, not constitutional — merely *having* a written constitution does not make a government constitutional (the USSR and many dictatorships had constitutions).

The devices of restraint in India: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, separation of powers, federalism, free elections and rule of law.
questions.tagging_note: Conceptual/definitional question on what constitutional government means (limited government, restraints on state power in favour of individual liberty). No 'political theory / concepts' topic exists in the vocabulary; POL-03 (salient features) is the closest genuine home, with POL-14 for the parliamentary/limited-government framing.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Statements 1 and 2 are near-mirror images of each other; verified against the page that they are in the printed order and not swapped.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी किसी राज्य के राज्यपाल को दी गई विवेकाधीन शक्तियाँ हैं?
1. भारत के राष्ट्रपति को, राष्ट्रपति शासन अधिरोपित करने के लिए रिपोर्ट भेजना
2. मंत्रियों की नियुक्ति करना
3. राज्य विधानमण्डल द्वारा पारित कतिपय विधेयकों को, भारत के राष्ट्रपति के विचार के लिए आरक्षित करना
4. राज्य सरकार के कार्य संचालन के लिए नियम बनाना
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
Statement-wise on the **Governor's discretionary powers** (Art. 163 — the Governor acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers *except* where the Constitution requires him to act in his discretion):

1. **Discretionary** — sending a report to the President recommending Art. 356 (President's Rule). Obviously so, since he is reporting against his own ministry.
2. **Not discretionary** — ministers are appointed **on the advice of the Chief Minister** (Art. 164). (Only appointing the CM in a hung house is a situational discretion — appointing *ministers* is not.)
3. **Discretionary** — reserving a Bill for the President's consideration under **Art. 200**; the proviso to Art. 200 even makes reservation *mandatory* where a Bill derogates from the High Court's powers.
4. **Not discretionary** — under Art. 166(3) the Governor makes rules for the more convenient transaction of business, but does so on ministerial advice.

**Statement 2 is the giveaway — ministers are always the CM's choice — which removes (a), (c) and (d)**, leaving 1 and 3.
questions.tagging_note: Governor's discretionary powers = POL-21; the Art 356 report limb touches POL-16 and reserving bills for the President touches Centre-State relations (POL-15).
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.

questions.stem: किसी अर्थव्यवस्था में यदि ब्याज की दर को घटाया जाता है, तो वह
options: अर्थव्यवस्था में निवेश व्यय को बढ़ाएगा
अर्थव्यवस्था में कुल बचत को बढ़ाएगा
questions.explanation_md:
A cut in the interest rate lowers the **cost of borrowing**, so firms find more projects profitable at the margin.

- **(a) wrong** — cheaper credit and a lower return on saving *raise* consumption, not lower it.
- **(b) wrong** — tax collection depends on income, output and tax rates, not directly on the policy rate.
- **(c) correct** — **investment demand is inversely related to the rate of interest**; this is the core transmission channel of easy money.
- **(d) wrong** — a lower reward for saving *discourages* saving; households shift towards spending.

One line to remember: rate down → borrowing cheap → **investment up**, saving down.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. राष्ट्रपति, भारत सरकार का कार्य अधिक सुविधापूर्वक किए जाने के लिए और मंत्रियों में उक्त कार्य के आबंटन के लिए नियम बनाएगा।
2. भारत सरकार की समस्त कार्यपालक कार्रवाइयाँ प्रधानमंत्री के नाम से की हुई कही जाएँगी।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
Both statements come from **Article 77** (Conduct of Business of the Government of India).

- **1 — correct.** Art. 77(3): the **President shall make rules** for the more convenient transaction of business of the Government of India and for its allocation among Ministers. These are the *Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules* and *(Transaction of Business) Rules*.
- **2 — wrong.** Art. 77(1): all executive action of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken **in the name of the President**, not the Prime Minister. (For a State, Art. 166 puts it in the Governor's name.)

The PM's name appears nowhere in Art. 77 — that alone kills statement 2. **Answer: 1 only.**
questions.tagging_note: Art 77 — conduct of business of GoI, allocation among ministers, and executive action expressed in the name of the President. Sits in Laxmikanth's President / Council of Ministers chapters, i.e. POL-17.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Statement 2 says 'प्रधानमंत्री के नाम से' on the page — this is the printed wording and the deliberate trap; do not correct it to राष्ट्रपति.

questions.stem:
भारत में अविश्वास प्रस्ताव के विषय में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. भारत के संविधान में किसी अविश्वास प्रस्ताव का कोई उल्लेख नहीं है।
2. अविश्वास प्रस्ताव केवल लोक सभा में ही पुरःस्थापित किया जा सकता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
- **1 — correct.** The Constitution **never uses the words "no-confidence motion"**. It only lays down collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha (Art. 75(3)). The motion itself lives in **Rule 198 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha**, and needs the support of at least **50 members** to be admitted.
- **2 — correct.** Because the government is responsible only to the **Lok Sabha**, a no-confidence motion can be moved **only in the Lok Sabha** — the Rajya Sabha cannot remove a government (it can pass a censure motion or discuss, but not a no-confidence motion).

**Answer: both 1 and 2.** Contrast: a *censure motion* states reasons and can be moved in either House; a *no-confidence motion* needs no reasons and is Lok Sabha only.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Statement 1 carries the negative 'नहीं'. The stem runs across the column break: statements 1-2 are at the foot of the left column on p.29, the lead-in and options are at the head of the right column.

questions.stem:
नीम के पेड़ के सन्दर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. कुछ जाति के कीटों और बरुथियों के प्रचुरोद्भवन को नियंत्रित करने के लिए नीम के तेल का प्रयोग कीटनाशक के रूप में किया जा सकता है।
2. नीम के बीजों का प्रयोग जैव-ईंधन और अस्पताल अपमार्जकों का निर्माण करने में होता है।
3. नीम के तेल का अनुप्रयोग औषधि उद्योग में होता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
Statements 1 and 3 are both about **नीम का तेल (neem oil)** and both are standard, uncontested facts. Statement 2 quietly changes the subject to **नीम के बीज (neem seeds)** and bundles two different products with "और". That is the whole question.

- **1 — correct.** Neem oil (azadirachtin and related limonoids) works as an antifeedant, repellent and insect growth regulator, and is a registered **acaricide** as well — so it controls both **कीट (insects)** and **बरुथी (mites)**. Do not reject this statement because mites are arachnids and not insects: the statement lists them separately, it does not call mites insects.
- **3 — correct.** Neem oil goes into the pharmaceutical industry as an antibacterial/antifungal ingredient and in Ayurvedic formulations. Uncontroversial.
- **2 — wrong, on one precise word: अपमार्जक.** An **अपमार्जक (detergent)** is a surfactant cleaning agent. What neem is actually known for in a hospital setting is being a **कीटाणुनाशक / रोगाणुनाशक (antiseptic / disinfectant)** — an antimicrobial, not a cleaning surfactant. UPSC has swapped a term of art for a near-neighbour: *disinfectant → detergent*. "Hospital detergents" manufactured from neem seeds is not a documented product category; neem as a hospital antiseptic is. Supporting point on the other half: India's biodiesel programme is built on **jatropha and pongamia (करंज)** seeds, not neem — neem oil appears in research papers as a candidate feedstock, not in manufacture at scale.

A compound statement joined by "और" is only as true as its **weaker half**. Even granting the biofuel clause, "अस्पताल अपमार्जक" sinks statement 2, and 2 is exactly what separates (c) from (d).

**Why (d) tempts and fails:** the solver reasons "neem soap is antibacterial, hospitals use neem-based washes, so 2 is fine" and marks all three. That reasoning proves neem is a **disinfectant ingredient**, which is not what statement 2 claims. It also silently upgrades *neem seeds* to *neem oil* — the two statements UPSC wrote correctly (1 and 3) both say तेल, and the one it wrote as a trap says बीज. When an examiner changes a noun mid-question, the change is the point.

**Method:** with 1 and 3 certain, options (a) and (b) die immediately and the question collapses to a single doubtful statement. In that position, read the doubtful statement at its most literal, and check every noun in it against the exact term you learnt. Do not mark it true because something *near* it is true.

**Durable:** neem oil → insecticide/acaricide + pharmaceutical use (both true). Neem in hospitals → **antiseptic**, not **detergent**. Biodiesel tree seeds in the Indian programme → **jatropha, pongamia**.
questions.tagging_note: Weak fit — the vocabulary has no topic for economic botany / commercial uses of plants (biopesticide, detergent, pharma feedstock). ENV-07 is the only species-level topic and ENV-16 covers biofuels only. Straddles ENV, SNT and GEO-17 agriculture. Real gap in the syllabus tree.

questions.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक प्रक्रम प्रकाश-संश्लेषण में सम्मिलित है?
options: स्थितिज ऊर्जा मुक्त होकर प्राप्यतम ऊर्जा बनती है
प्राप्यतम ऊर्जा, स्थितिज ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित होती है और संचित हो जाती है
भोजन ऑक्सीकृत होकर कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड और जल मुक्त करता है
ऑक्सीजन ली जाती है तथा कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड और जलवाष्प बाहर निकलते हैं
questions.explanation_md:
Photosynthesis is an **energy-storing (endergonic, anabolic)** process: light energy → chemical energy locked in glucose bonds.

- **(a) wrong** — that describes energy being *released*, i.e. respiration/catabolism.
- **(b) correct** — **free (available) light energy is trapped and converted into potential chemical energy, which is stored** in carbohydrate.
- **(c) wrong** — oxidation of food releasing CO₂ and water is **respiration**.
- **(d) wrong** — taking in O₂ and giving out CO₂ and water vapour is **respiration/transpiration**, the reverse of photosynthesis (which takes in CO₂ and releases O₂).

Test: photosynthesis *stores* energy; respiration *releases* it.
questions.tagging_note: SNT-01 is scoped as 'cell, genetics, human systems, nutrition' — plant physiology / photosynthesis has no dedicated topic, so this is filed under basic biology by default.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Options (a) and (b) are inversions of each other; verified in printed order.

questions.stem:
किसी व्यक्ति के जीवमितीय पहचान हेतु, अंगुली-छाप क्रमवीक्षण के अलावा, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/से प्रयोग में लाया जा सकता है/लाए जा सकते हैं?
1. परितारिका क्रमवीक्षण
2. दृष्टिपटल क्रमवीक्षण
3. वाक् अभिज्ञान
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
Biometrics = any measurable physiological or behavioural trait unique to a person. **All three qualify.**

- **1 — Iris scan:** patterns of the coloured ring around the pupil; used in **Aadhaar** enrolment along with fingerprints.
- **2 — Retina scan:** the blood-vessel pattern at the back of the eye; one of the most accurate biometrics, though intrusive.
- **3 — Voice recognition:** a **behavioural biometric** (voiceprint), used in phone banking and access control.

Other valid biometrics: face, gait, palm/vein pattern, DNA, signature dynamics. **Answer: 1, 2 and 3.**
questions.tagging_note: Biometrics (iris, retina, voice recognition) is not named in any topic; SNT-09 IT/computing is the nearest home, with SNT-10 (data protection, Aadhaar-adjacent) as the secondary.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/से कथन पौधों के कायिक प्रवर्धन के सम्बन्ध में सही है/हैं?
1. कायिक प्रवर्धन क्लोनीय जनसंख्या को उत्पन्न करता है।
2. कायिक प्रवर्धन विषाणुओं का निष्प्रभावन करने में सहायक है।
3. कायिक प्रवर्धन वर्ष के अधिकतर भाग में चल सकता है।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
- **1 — correct.** Vegetative (asexual) propagation involves only mitosis, so the offspring are genetically identical — a **clonal population**.
- **2 — wrong.** This is the deciding statement. Vegetative propagation **carries viruses forward**, because viral particles travel in the vascular tissue of the cutting/tuber/graft; potato, sugarcane and banana virus loads build up exactly this way. Virus *elimination* needs **meristem-tip culture / thermotherapy**, not ordinary vegetative propagation.
- **3 — correct.** It does not depend on flowering or seed set, so cuttings, layering and grafting can be done through **most of the year**.

**Answer: 1 and 3 only.**
questions.tagging_note: Vegetative propagation / clonal populations and virus transmission — plant reproduction is not explicitly in SNT-01's scope; SNT-03 covers the tissue-culture side and GEO-17 the horticultural application.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित युग्मों में से कौन-सा/से सही सुमेलित है/हैं?

| | अन्तरिक्ष यान | प्रयोजन |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | कैसिनी-हाइगेन्स | शुक्र की परिक्रमा करना और दत्त का पृथ्वी तक संचारण करना |
| 2. | मेसेंजर | बुध का मानचित्रण और अन्वेषण |
| 3. | वॉयेजर 1 और 2 | बाह्य सौर परिवार का अन्वेषण |

नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
- **1 — wrong.** **Cassini–Huygens went to Saturn**, not Venus: NASA/ESA mission, orbited Saturn 2004–2017, and the Huygens probe landed on **Titan** in January 2005.
- **2 — correct.** **MESSENGER** (NASA) orbited **Mercury** from 2011 to 2015, mapping the entire surface — first spacecraft ever to orbit Mercury.
- **3 — correct.** **Voyager 1 and 2** (1977) explored the **outer solar system** — Jupiter, Saturn, and for Voyager 2 also Uranus and Neptune — and have since crossed into interstellar space.

**Answer: 2 and 3 only.** Venus missions to remember instead: Magellan, Venus Express, Akatsuki.
questions.tagging_note: Cassini-Huygens, MESSENGER, Voyager are non-ISRO planetary missions, so SNT-06 ('global missions') rather than SNT-05, which is ISRO-scoped.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित युग्मों पर विचार कीजिए :

| | क्षेत्र | किसके उत्पादन के लिए जाना जाता है |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | किन्नौर | सुपारी |
| 2. | मेवात | आम |
| 3. | कोरोमण्डल | सोयाबीन |

उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से युग्म सही सुमेलित है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
All three pairs are wrong — a classic "None" question.

- **1 — wrong.** **Kinnaur (Himachal Pradesh)** is a cold, high-altitude district famous for **apples, chilgoza (pine nuts) and grapes**. Arecanut (supari) is a humid-tropical crop — Karnataka, Kerala, Assam.
- **2 — wrong.** **Mewat (Haryana/Rajasthan)** is a semi-arid tract known for **pearl millet, mustard and dairy/livestock**, not mango. Mango belts: Malihabad, Ratnagiri, Malda, Krishnagiri.
- **3 — wrong.** The **Coromandel coast** (Tamil Nadu–Andhra east coast) grows **rice, groundnut, tobacco and sugarcane**. **Soybean is a Malwa-plateau crop — Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra**, which need a well-drained black-soil interior, not a coastal plain.

**Answer: None.**

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/से रासायनिक परिवर्तन का/के उदाहरण है/हैं?
1. सोडियम क्लोराइड का क्रिस्टलन
2. बर्फ का गलन
3. दुग्ध आस्कंदन
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
Test: does a **new substance with new chemical composition** form, and is the change **irreversible**?

- **1 — physical.** Crystallisation of sodium chloride from solution is only a change of state/arrangement; the NaCl is chemically unchanged and redissolves.
- **2 — physical.** Melting of ice is a phase change, H₂O → H₂O; refreeze and you get the ice back.
- **3 — chemical.** **Curdling/souring of milk: bacteria convert lactose into lactic acid**, which coagulates casein. New substances, irreversible — a chemical change.

**Answer: 3 only.**
questions.tagging_note: Physical vs chemical change — sits squarely in SNT-13 'everyday physics and chemistry'.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.

questions.stem: केन्द्र और राज्यों के बीच होने वाले विवादों का निर्णय करने की भारत के उच्चतम न्यायालय की शक्ति किसके अन्तर्गत आती है?
questions.explanation_md:
**Article 131 — exclusive original jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court covers disputes between (i) Centre and one or more States, (ii) Centre and States on one side vs States on the other, (iii) two or more States — provided the dispute involves a question of **legal right**, not a political grievance.

- (a) Advisory = Art. 143 (President refers a question of law/public importance; opinion not binding).
- (b) Appellate = Arts. 132–136 (constitutional, civil, criminal, special leave).
- (d) Writ = Art. 32, for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (and this is *concurrent* with High Courts under Art. 226, not exclusive).

Note the exclusions from Art. 131: pre-Constitution treaties/agreements still in force, inter-State water disputes (Art. 262), and matters referred to the Finance Commission.
