questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित तकनीकों/परिघटनाओं पर विचार कीजिए :
1. फल वाले पादपों में मुकुलन और रोपण
2. कोशिकाद्रव्यी नर बन्ध्यता
3. जीन नीरवता
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से ट्रांसजेनिक फसलों को बनाने में प्रयुक्त होता है/होते हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
Transgenic = a **foreign gene inserted** into the plant genome.

1. **Budding and grafting — NO.** Pure vegetative/conventional propagation of fruit plants (mango, citrus). No gene transfer, no new DNA. This single verdict decides the question.
2. **Cytoplasmic male sterility — YES (as used today).** CMS itself is a natural mitochondrial trait, but male sterility for hybrid seed is now engineered transgenically — the *barnase–barstar* system inserts a ribonuclease gene under a tapetum-specific promoter (used in GM mustard, DMH-11).
3. **Gene silencing — YES.** Antisense RNA / RNAi is a standard transgenic tool: Flavr Savr tomato (delayed ripening), virus- and nematode-resistant crops, low-acrylamide potato.

**Since 1 is out, only option (b) survives** — no need to agonise over 2.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Options (b) and (c) are printed without 'केवल' on the page.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. मक्का का मण्ड के उत्पादन के लिए प्रयोग किया जा सकता है।
2. मक्का से निष्कर्षित तेल जैव-डीजल के लिए फीडस्टॉक हो सकता है।
3. मक्का के प्रयोग से एल्कोहॉली पेय उत्पन्न किया जा सकता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
All three uses of maize are real — maize is the classic "food, feed, fuel" crop.

1. **Starch — correct.** Corn starch is the world's main commercial starch source; also gives corn syrup, dextrose, and biodegradable plastic (PLA).
2. **Corn oil as biodiesel feedstock — correct.** Oil from the maize germ is a triglyceride and can be transesterified to biodiesel; US ethanol plants recover "distillers corn oil" specifically for this.
3. **Alcoholic beverage — correct.** Bourbon whiskey, American corn whiskey, and traditional *chicha* are maize-based; maize is also the leading feedstock for fuel ethanol in the USA.

**All three ⇒ (d).**
questions.tagging_note: Straddles subjects: uses of maize (starch, ethanol, oil as biodiesel feedstock). No topic covers crop utilisation / agro-processing directly; GEO-17 (India agriculture: crops) is the nearest, ENV-16 carries the biofuel half.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.

questions.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक जीव, अन्य तीन जीवों के वर्ग का **नहीं** है?
questions.explanation_md:
All four are arthropods, but **crab is a crustacean; mite, scorpion and spider are arachnids**.

| | Arachnida (mite, scorpion, spider) | Crustacea (crab) |
|---|---|---|
| Legs | **4 pairs** | 5 pairs (decapods) |
| Antennae | **None** | 2 pairs |
| Body | Cephalothorax + abdomen | Cephalothorax + abdomen, with gills |
| Respiration | Book lungs / tracheae | Gills |

Quick rule for such questions: **count the legs and look for antennae** — the odd one out is the crab.
questions.tagging_note: Odd-one-out on animal classification (crab is a crustacean; mite, scorpion, spider are arachnids). The vocabulary has no animal taxonomy/classification topic — SNT-01 'Basic biology' is the nearest fit but its stated scope (cell, genetics, human systems, nutrition) does not actually include this. Real gap in the syllabus tree.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. 'नहीं' is printed in bold on the page and is preserved in the stem.

questions.stem: भारत के उच्चतम न्यायालय में न्यायाधीशों की संख्या में वृद्धि करने की शक्ति किसमें निहित है?
questions.explanation_md:
**Article 124(1): the Supreme Court shall consist of a Chief Justice and "such number of other Judges as Parliament may by law prescribe"** — until Parliament legislates, seven other judges.

Parliament has done this through the **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956**, amended repeatedly: 10 → 13 → 17 → 25 → 30 (1986) → **33 + CJI = 34 (2019 amendment)**.

- The President only *appoints* judges (Art. 124(2)); he cannot change the sanctioned strength.
- The CJI is consulted on appointments and heads the collegium, but does not fix strength.
- The Law Commission is advisory only.

Contrast: strength of a **High Court** is fixed by the **President**, not Parliament.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.

questions.stem:
भारत के निम्नलिखित नगरों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. भद्राचलम
2. चंदेरी
3. कांचीपुरम
4. करनाल
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-कौन से पारम्परिक साड़ी/वस्त्र उत्पादन के लिए सुख्यात हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
The deciding word is **पारम्परिक (traditional)**: the stem asks for towns with a *handloom weaving tradition the cloth is named after*, not simply towns with industry. Only two of the four qualify.

- **1. भद्राचलम (Bhadrachalam) — no.** A temple town on the Godavari (Sri Sita Ramachandraswamy). Its modern fame is a **paper and paperboard mill**, not cloth. No saree carries its name. Telangana's weaving towns are Pochampally, Gadwal, Narayanpet and Siddipet.
- **2. चंदेरी (Chanderi) — yes.** Ashoknagar district, MP; the light silk-cotton **Chanderi saree**, GI-registered.
- **3. कांचीपुरम (Kancheepuram) — yes.** The heavy zari **Kanchipuram silk saree**, GI-registered.
- **4. करनाल (Karnal) — no.** Haryana; known for the National Dairy Research Institute and agricultural research, not textiles.

Answer **(b) केवल 2 और 3**.

Why **(c)** fails: it adds Bhadrachalam on two false leads — the *temple town, therefore silk* reflex borrowed from Kanchipuram and Varanasi, and a hazy memory of Bhadrachalam as an industrial town. It is an industrial town, but the industry is **paper**, not handloom. Note the structure: Karnal appears only in (d), so once you rule Karnal out the entire question collapses to a single call — is Bhadrachalam a weaving centre? It is not, so (b), not (c).

Durable: a traditional textile town is one whose **name the fabric carries** — Chanderi, Kanchipuram, Pochampally, Maheshwar, Paithan, Venkatagiri, Bhagalpur. If no saree is named after the town, it does not belong on the list.
questions.tagging_note: Cities known for traditional sarees/textiles (Bhadrachalam, Chanderi, Kanchipuram, Karnal). No topic covers handicrafts/handloom textiles; ART-10 is the nearest only because it carries GI tags, and GEO-19 only because textiles are an industry. Genuine gap: crafts and textile traditions are not in the vocabulary.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages.
questions.review_flag: Official key says b, worked solution said c (medium confidence).

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित युग्मों पर विचार कीजिए :

| | राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग | इससे जुड़े शहर |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | NH 4 | चेन्नई और हैदराबाद |
| 2. | NH 6 | मुम्बई और कोलकाता |
| 3. | NH 15 | अहमदाबाद और जोधपुर |

उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से युग्म सही सुमेलित है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
All three pairs are wrong (old NH numbering, pre-2010 renumbering).

1. **NH 4 — wrong.** Mumbai/Thane → Pune → Satara → Belgaum → **Bengaluru → Chennai**. It never touches Hyderabad. Chennai–Hyderabad is not NH 4; Hyderabad sits on NH 7 (Varanasi–Kanyakumari) and NH 9 (Pune–Machilipatnam).
2. **NH 6 — wrong.** Runs **Hazira (Surat) → Dhule → Nagpur → Raipur → Sambalpur → Kolkata**. Its western terminus is in Gujarat, not Mumbai (Mumbai links to it via NH 3).
3. **NH 15 — wrong.** The western-border highway: **Pathankot → Amritsar → Bathinda → Bikaner → Jaisalmer → Barmer → Samakhiali (Kutch)**. It misses both Ahmedabad and Jodhpur; Jodhpur lay on NH 65 (Ambala–Pali).

**Exam shortcut:** NH 4's Mumbai–Chennai identity is the most familiar fact on the page — once statement 1 falls, options (a) and (c) go, and NH 15 being a border highway rules out (b), leaving **(d) None**.
questions.tagging_note: Format: three numbered National Highway–cities pairs asking which are correctly matched. Labelled 'pairs' rather than stmt_1_2_3 because the items are pairs, and match_list is reserved for List I / List II.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Highway numbers verified against the page: NH 4, NH 6, NH 15.

questions.stem:
निम्नलिखित अन्तर्राष्ट्रीय करारों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. खाद्य एवं कृषि हेतु पादप आनुवंशिक संसाधनों के विषय में अन्तर्राष्ट्रीय संधि
2. मरुभवन का सामना करने हेतु संयुक्त राष्ट्र अभिसमय
3. विश्व विरासत अभिसमय
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से जैव-विविधता से सम्बन्ध रखता है/रखते हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
The question asks what is **related to** biodiversity, not what is exclusively about it — so read generously.

1. **ITPGRFA (Plant Treaty, 2001, FAO)** — directly agrobiodiversity: multilateral system for access to 64 crops, Farmers' Rights, benefit sharing. India's PPV&FR Act is its domestic counterpart. **Related.**
2. **UNCCD (1994)** — one of the three **Rio conventions** with CBD and UNFCCC; combating desertification and land degradation is explicitly aimed at restoring degraded ecosystems, hence **related** (its text speaks of conservation and sustainable use of land, water and biological resources).
3. **World Heritage Convention (1972, UNESCO)** — protects **natural** as well as cultural heritage; India's natural sites include Kaziranga, Manas, Sundarbans, Nanda Devi and the Western Ghats. **Related.**

**All three ⇒ (d).** Nothing here is purely cultural or purely industrial, so no statement can be excluded.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. The stem runs across the column break: statements 1-3 are at the foot of the left column on p.35 and the lead-in plus options are at the head of the right column.

questions.stem:
'पृथ्वी काल' के सन्दर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. यह UNEP तथा UNESCO का उपक्रमण है।
2. यह एक आन्दोलन है, जिसमें प्रतिभागी प्रतिवर्ष एक निश्चित दिन, एक घण्टे के लिए बिजली बन्द कर देते हैं।
3. यह जलवायु परिवर्तन और पृथ्वी को बचाने की आवश्यकता के बारे में जागरूकता लाने वाला आन्दोलन है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
1. **UNEP + UNESCO — WRONG.** **Earth Hour is a WWF initiative**, begun in **Sydney in 2007**. This single error removes options (a) and (d).
2. **Correct.** Individuals, households and businesses switch off non-essential lights for **one hour**, on the last Saturday of March, 8:30–9:30 p.m. local time.
3. **Correct.** Its stated purpose is symbolic — raising **awareness of climate change** and of the need to protect the planet; the energy actually saved in that hour is negligible and never the point.

**2 and 3 only ⇒ (c).**

Don't confuse with **Earth Day (22 April)** or **World Environment Day (5 June, UNEP)**.
questions.tagging_note: Question is on Earth Hour — a WWF public-awareness campaign, not a treaty or a science point. Nothing in the vocabulary covers environmental awareness movements/campaigns; ENV-13 (climate governance) and ENV-12 (climate change) are the least-bad fits. Real gap in the syllabus tree.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. UNEP and UNESCO are printed in Latin script on the page.

questions.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक आहार शृंखला का सही क्रम है?
questions.explanation_md:
**Diatoms → crustaceans → herring.**

Energy must flow **producer → primary consumer → secondary consumer**:

- **Diatoms** = phytoplankton, the photosynthetic **producers** of the sea, so they must come first — that alone eliminates (b) and (d).
- **Crustaceans** (copepods, krill) = zooplankton grazing on diatoms = primary consumers.
- **Herring** = a small fish feeding on zooplankton = secondary consumer, and being much larger it cannot be eaten by copepods — which eliminates (c).

Remember: each step loses ~90% of energy (**10% law**), so a food chain runs small-and-numerous to large-and-few.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. All four options are permutations of the same three terms; order verified option by option against the page.

questions.stem: 1905 में लॉर्ड कर्ज़न द्वारा किया गया बंगाल का विभाजन कब तक बना रहा?
options: प्रथम विश्वयुद्ध तक, जिसमें अंग्रेजों को भारतीय सैनिकों की आवश्यकता पड़ी और विभाजन समाप्त किया गया
सम्राट जॉर्ज पंचम द्वारा दिल्ली में 1911 के शाही दरबार में कर्ज़न के अधिनियम को निराकृत किये जाने तक
महात्मा गाँधी द्वारा अपना सविनय अवज्ञा आन्दोलन आरम्भ करने तक
भारत के 1947 में हुए विभाजन तक, जब पूर्वी बंगाल, पूर्वी पाकिस्तान बन गया
questions.explanation_md:
**The 1905 Partition of Bengal was annulled by King George V at the Delhi Durbar of December 1911.**

- Curzon's partition took effect **16 Oct 1905**; the Swadeshi and Boycott movement grew out of the protest against it.
- At the 1911 Durbar the annulment was announced **together with the shift of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi** — Bengal was reunited on linguistic lines, while Bihar–Orissa and Assam were carved out separately.
- (a) is wrong — the reversal came three years *before* WWI. (c) Civil Disobedience began 1930. (d) The 1947 partition of Bengal was a fresh, separate event.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Years verified: 1905 in the stem, 1911 in option (b), 1947 in option (d).

questions.stem: स्वतंत्रता आन्दोलन के इतिहास में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय काँग्रेस का 1929 का अधिवेशन इसलिए महत्त्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि इस अधिवेशन में
options: काँग्रेस के उद्देश्य के तौर पर स्व-शासन प्राप्ति की घोषणा की गई
काँग्रेस के लक्ष्य के तौर पर पूर्ण स्वराज प्राप्ति को स्वीकृत किया गया
लन्दन में गोल मेज़ सम्मेलन में भागीदारी करने का निर्णय लिया गया
questions.explanation_md:
**Lahore session, December 1929 (President: Jawaharlal Nehru) adopted *Purna Swaraj* — complete independence — as the Congress goal.**

- The tricolour was hoisted on the bank of the Ravi on **31 Dec 1929**, and **26 January 1930** was observed as the first Independence Day.
- Dominion status/self-government was the older demand (Nehru Report 1928 asked for Dominion Status; its one-year ultimatum lapsed at Lahore).
- Non-Cooperation began at the **Nagpur session, 1920**; the Round Table Conference decision came later (Congress attended only the Second RTC, 1931, after the Gandhi–Irwin Pact).
questions.tagging_note: Lahore session 1929 (Purna Swaraj) sits in HIS-11; HIS-16 added because the question is fundamentally about which INC session decided what.
questions.transcription_note: Hindi half of the bilingual booklet; English version is not on these pages. Year 1929 verified against the page.

questions.stem:
विख्यात सत्रीया नृत्य के सन्दर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. सत्रीया, संगीत, नृत्य तथा अभिनय का सम्मिश्रण है।
2. यह असम के वैष्णवों की शताब्दियों पुरानी जीवन्त परम्परा है।
3. यह तुलसीदास, कबीर और मीराबाई द्वारा रचित भक्ति-गीतों के शास्त्रीय रागों तथा तालों पर आधारित है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
**Statement 3 is the deciding error — Sattriya is set to Sankardeva's *Borgeets*, not to Tulsidas, Kabir or Mirabai.**

1. **Correct** — Sattriya blends music (*sangeet*), dance (*nritya*) and drama/acting (*abhinaya*), growing out of the *Ankiya Naat* one-act plays.
2. **Correct** — a living tradition of the **Vaishnava *sattras* (monasteries) of Assam**, begun by Srimanta Sankardeva in the 15th century; recognised as a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in **2000**.
3. **Wrong** — its lyrical base is the Borgeets and Ankiya plays of Sankardeva and Madhavdeva, in Brajavali; the north-Indian bhakti poets are not its source.

Hence 1 and 2 only.

questions.explanation_md:
**1 Chaitra of the Saka-based National Calendar falls on 22 March in a normal year (21 March in a leap year).**

- Adopted **22 March 1957** on the recommendation of the Calendar Reform Committee (chair: **Meghnad Saha**); the Saka era begins in **78 CE**.
- The year opens the day after the **vernal equinox**, so Chaitra has 30 days in a normal year and 31 in a leap year — which is why the leap-year start slides back to 21 March.
- Used in the *Gazette of India*, AIR news broadcasts and government calendars alongside the Gregorian date.
questions.tagging_note: GAP: no topic in the vocabulary covers Indian calendars/eras (Saka samvat, the National Calendar). ART-10 is used only as the culture catch-all; the 22 March answer rests on the vernal equinox, which is the one genuine hook into GEO-01. Worth a syllabus-tree entry if calendar/era questions recur.

| 2. प्रस्तर पर उत्कीर्ण विष्णु के वराह अवतार की विशाल प्रतिमा जिसमें वह देवी पृथ्वी को गहरे विक्षुब्ध सागर से उबारते दर्शाए गए हैं | माउंट आबू |
| 3. विशाल गोलाश्मों पर उत्कीर्ण ''अर्जुन की तपस्या''/''गंगा-अवतरण'' | मामल्लपुरम |

उपर्युक्त युग्मों में से कौन-सा/से सही सुमेलित है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
**The Varaha panel belongs to Udayagiri (Vidisha, MP) — Mount Abu is Dilwara *Jain* marble temples, so pair 2 breaks.**

1. **Correct** — the colossal reclining **Mahaparinirvana Buddha in Cave 26 at Ajanta**, with celestial beings above and mourning disciples carved below.
2. **Wrong** — the giant rock-cut Varaha raising Bhudevi from the ocean is the Gupta-period panel at **Udayagiri caves**; a famous Varaha relief also exists at Mamallapuram. Mount Abu has no such sculpture.
3. **Correct** — **"Arjuna's Penance" / "Descent of the Ganga"** is the huge Pallava open-air bas-relief on twin boulders at **Mamallapuram**.

Hence 1 and 3 only.

ART-05 is named for the Gandhara/Mathura/Amaravati schools, so it is a loose home for famous individual sculptures — that is the nearest fit rather than an exact one.

questions.explanation_md:
**Ghadar was a revolutionary organisation of Indians (largely Punjabi emigrants) headquartered at San Francisco, USA.**

- Founded **1913** as the Hindi Association of the Pacific Coast; leaders **Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha**; its paper *Ghadar* was published in Urdu, Punjabi and other languages.
- The **Komagata Maru** episode (1914) and the outbreak of WWI triggered the plan for an armed rising in Punjab in **February 1915**, betrayed by Kirpal Singh and crushed (Lahore Conspiracy Case).
- Distractors: the **Berlin Committee** (Indian Independence Committee) was the Germany-based body; **Tashkent** is linked to M.N. Roy and the Communist Party of India (1920); Singapore relates to the later INA/1915 Singapore mutiny.

questions.explanation_md:
**Kalaripayattu is an ancient martial art, still a living tradition in Kerala and adjoining parts of south India.**

- Practised in a *kalari* (training pit/arena) under a *gurukkal*; stages run from body conditioning (*meithari*) to wooden weapons (*kolthari*), metal weapons (*angathari*, including the flexible *urumi*) and bare-hand combat (*verumkai*).
- It is closely tied to **marma** (vital-point) knowledge and traditional Ayurvedic massage, and is credited with influencing Kathakali's body training.
- Not a bhakti sect, not a metalcraft, not a dance-drama — Kerala's north Malabar dance-ritual form is **Theyyam**.

questions.explanation_md:
**Mohiniyattam is Kerala's classical dance, not Odisha's — Odisha's is Odissi.**

1. **Correct** — **Garba** is Gujarat's circular folk dance around a perforated earthen lamp-pot (*garbo*), performed at Navratri; Dandiya-Raas is its stick variant.
2. **Wrong** — **Mohiniyattam**, the lasya-dominant solo dance in the *mohini* (enchantress) idiom with off-white and gold costume, belongs to **Kerala**.
3. **Correct** — **Yakshagana** is the all-night folk theatre of coastal **Karnataka** (Udupi–Dakshina Kannada), with elaborate headgear, *himmela* orchestra and *bhagavata* narrator.

Hence 1 and 3 only.

उपर्युक्त युग्मों में से कौन-सा/से सही सुमेलित है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
**Nako, with its Lotsava (Lhotsava) Lhakhang, is in the Hangrang valley of Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh — not the Zanskar valley.**

1. **Correct** — **Tabo** monastery (founded 996 CE, "Ajanta of the Himalayas") stands in the **Spiti valley**, Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh; an ASI-protected complex of mud-brick temples with Indo-Tibetan murals.
2. **Wrong** — Nako's temple group is Kinnaur; **Zanskar** lies in the Kargil district of Ladakh (Karsha, Phuktal monasteries).
3. **Correct** — the **Alchi** Choskor complex is on the Indus in **Ladakh**, famous for 11th–12th century Kashmiri-style murals and, unusually, built on flat ground rather than a hilltop.

Hence 1 and 3 only.
questions.tagging_note: GAP: nothing in the vocabulary covers Himalayan Buddhist monastic sites (Tabo, Nako, Alchi). ART-01 is the nearest fit via viharas/monastic architecture, and the question is really location recall, hence GEO-24. ANM-04 was rejected — it is doctrinal Buddhism, not site geography.

निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
1. 'बीजक' सन्त दादू दयाल के उपदेशों का एक संकलन है।
2. पुष्टि मार्ग के दर्शन को मध्वाचार्य ने प्रतिपादित किया।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanation_md:
**Both are misattributed — *Bijak* is Kabir's, and Pushti Marg is Vallabhacharya's.**

1. **Wrong** — the **Bijak** is the compilation of **Kabir's** verses (*sakhi, ramaini, shabad*), the principal scripture of the Kabirpanth. Dadu Dayal's followers (Dadupanth) preserve the **Dadu Vani / Dadu Bani**.
2. **Wrong** — **Pushti Marg**, the "path of grace" centred on Shrinathji and Krishna-bhakti with *Shuddhadvaita* philosophy, was founded by **Vallabhacharya** (1479–1531). **Madhvacharya** propounded **Dvaita** (dualism) in the 13th century.

Hence neither 1 nor 2.

questions.stem:
महारानी विक्टोरिया की उद्घोषणा (1858) का उद्देश्य क्या था?
1. भारतीय राज्यों को ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य में मिलाने के किसी भी विचार का परित्याग करना
2. भारतीय प्रशासन को ब्रिटिश क्राउन के अन्तर्गत रखना
3. भारत के साथ ईस्ट इन्डिया कम्पनी के व्यापार का नियमन करना

नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
Queen Victoria's Proclamation, read out by Lord Canning at Allahabad, 1 Nov 1858.

1. **Abandon annexation** — ✅ It promised to respect the rights, dignity and honour of native princes and desired "no extension of our present territorial possessions" — i.e. the **Doctrine of Lapse was given up** and adoption rights were conceded.
2. **Indian administration under the Crown** — ✅ This is the whole point: the Government of India Act 1858 abolished the Company's rule and transferred power to the Crown, with a Secretary of State for India.
3. **Regulate the Company's trade** — ❌ **The East India Company's commercial functions had already been ended by the Charter Act of 1833**; by 1858 the Company was being wound up entirely, so there was no trade left to regulate.

Only 1 and 2 → (a).
questions.tagging_note: Queen Victoria's Proclamation / GoI Act 1858 sits at the end of HIS-03's 1773-1858 constitutional span; HIS-04 added because the Proclamation is the direct aftermath of the 1857 Revolt.
questions.transcription_note: HINDI TEXT ONLY — English facing page not extracted. See note on Q85.

questions.explanation_md:
**Ibadat Khana = the "House of Worship" built by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575, where *he himself* held debates with theologians of many faiths.**

- Started as debates among Sunni ulema only; from 1578 opened to **Shias, Sufis, Hindus, Jains (Hiravijaya Suri), Zoroastrians (Dastur Meherji Rana) and Jesuits (Aquaviva, Monserrate)**.
- These discussions fed into the **Mahzar (1579)** and **Din-i-Ilahi / Tauhid-i-Ilahi (1582)**.
- Option (d) is the trap: it drops Akbar and makes it a nobles-only room — the debates were presided over by the emperor, so (c).

questions.stem:
भारत की खाद्य एवं पोषण सुरक्षा के सन्दर्भ में विभिन्न फसलों की 'बीज प्रतिस्थापन दरों' को बढ़ाने से भविष्य के खाद्य उत्पादन लक्ष्यों को प्राप्त करने में मदद मिलती है। किन्तु इसके अपेक्षाकृत बड़े/विस्तृत कार्यान्वयन में क्या बाध्यता है/बाध्यताएँ हैं?
1. कोई भी राष्ट्रीय बीज नीति नहीं बनी है।
2. निजी क्षेत्र की बीज कम्पनियों की, उद्यान-कृषि फसलों की रोपण सामग्रियों और सब्ज़ियों के गुणता वाले बीजों की पूर्ति में कोई सहभागिता नहीं है।
3. निम्न मूल्य एवं उच्च परिमाण वाली फसलों के मामले में गुणता वाले बीजों के बारे में माँग-पूर्ति अन्तराल है।

नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
Seed Replacement Rate (SRR) = share of area sown with certified/quality seed instead of farm-saved seed.

1. "No national seed policy" — ❌ India has had a **National Seed Policy, 2002** (plus Seeds Act 1966, Seeds Control Order 1983).
2. "Private sector has no role in vegetable seeds / horticultural planting material" — ❌ The opposite: **private companies dominate hybrid vegetable seed and horticultural planting material**, because margins there are high.
3. Demand–supply gap for **low-value, high-volume crops** — ✅ Exactly the constraint: self-pollinated bulky crops like **wheat, paddy, pulses** are unattractive to private firms (farmers re-use saved seed, seed is heavy and cheap), so the public sector must supply them and falls short.

Only 3 → (b). Rule of thumb: statements with absolutes like "no policy exists" / "no participation" are almost always wrong.
questions.tagging_note: Straddles ECO/GEO. Seed replacement rate, national seed policy and quality-seed supply are not named in any topic; ECO-14 (agri inputs/policy) is the closest, GEO-17 (crops, cropping patterns) the secondary fit. A dedicated 'agricultural inputs — seeds, fertilisers' topic is missing from the tree.

'पारिस्थितिक-संवेदी क्षेत्रों' के सन्दर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
1. पारिस्थितिक-संवेदी क्षेत्र वे क्षेत्र हैं, जिन्हें वन्यजीव (संरक्षण) अधिनियम, 1972 के अधीन घोषित किया गया है।
2. पारिस्थितिक-संवेदी क्षेत्र को घोषित करने का प्रयोजन है, उन क्षेत्रों में केवल कृषि को छोड़कर सभी मानव क्रियाओं पर प्रतिबन्ध लगाना।

नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
1. ❌ **Eco-Sensitive Zones are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** (Rule 5 of the EPA Rules, 1986), not the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. National parks and sanctuaries come under the 1972 Act; the ESZ is the cushion *around* them.
2. ❌ ESZs **regulate, they do not ban all activity**. The MoEFCC guidelines classify activities as **prohibited** (commercial mining, saw mills, major polluting industries, big hydel projects), **regulated** (felling, hotels, construction) and **permitted** (ongoing agriculture and horticulture, rainwater harvesting, organic farming). So it is not "everything banned except agriculture".

Neither correct → (d). ESZ extent: normally up to 10 km around a PA, but can be more.
questions.tagging_note: Eco-sensitive zones are not listed by name; ENV-06 (protected-area categories) is the nearest, with ENV-09 for the EPA 1986 vs WPA 1972 statutory-source distinction the question actually turns on.

1. ❌ The **Animal Welfare Board of India was set up in 1962 under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960** (Section 4) — not the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. It was the first such body in the world; now under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying.
2. ✅ **NTCA is statutory** — created by the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2006 (post-Sariska, on the Tiger Task Force's advice), chaired by the Environment Minister; it approves tiger reserves and Project Tiger.
3. ✅ **NGRBA (2009) was chaired by the Prime Minister**, constituted under Section 3 of the EPA 1986, declaring Ganga the National River. *(Post-2016 it has been replaced by the National Ganga Council, also PM-chaired — the answer is unchanged.)*

2 and 3 → (b).

questions.explanation_md:
1. **Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) → scurvy** ✅ — bleeding gums, poor collagen synthesis and wound healing.
2. **Vitamin D (calciferol) → rickets** in children, osteomalacia in adults ✅.
3. **Vitamin E (tocopherol) → NOT night blindness** ❌ — **night blindness (nyctalopia) is a Vitamin A deficiency**; vitamin E deficiency causes haemolysis of RBCs and neurological/muscle problems.

Only 1 and 2 → (a). Quick recall: A – night blindness/xerophthalmia; B1 – beri-beri; B3 – pellagra; B9/B12 – anaemia; C – scurvy; D – rickets; K – clotting failure.

1. वे पर्यावरण में संचित हो सकते हैं तथा जल और मृदा को संदूषित कर सकते हैं।
2. वे खाद्य शृंखलाओं में प्रविष्ट हो सकते हैं।
3. वे मुक्त मूलकों के उत्पादन को विमोचित कर सकते हैं।

नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.explanation_md:
All three concerns are real and well documented for engineered nanoparticles (nano-silver, TiO₂, ZnO, carbon nanotubes) used in paints, cosmetics, sunscreens, textiles and packaging.

1. ✅ They are **persistent and not easily degraded**; discharged in effluent they accumulate in sludge, soil and water bodies.
2. ✅ Being ultra-fine they are taken up by bacteria, plants and plankton and **bioaccumulate up the food chain**.
3. ✅ **The huge surface-area-to-volume ratio makes them catalytically reactive, generating reactive oxygen species (free radicals)** — this is the main mechanism of nanotoxicity, causing oxidative stress, DNA and membrane damage.

All three → (d). When every statement in a "why is there concern" question is a plausible harm, "all of the above" is usually right.
questions.tagging_note: Nanoparticles are SNT-11; ENV-11 added because statements 1 and 2 are pure soil/water contamination and food-chain bioaccumulation.

questions.explanation_md:
**World Economic Outlook (WEO) is the IMF's flagship report**, released twice a year (April and October) with updates in January and July, carrying global and country GDP growth projections.

Don't confuse the publishers:
- **IMF** — World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report, Fiscal Monitor.
- **World Bank** — World Development Report, Ease of Doing Business (till 2021), Global Economic Prospects.
- **UNDP** — Human Development Report.
- **WEF** — Global Competitiveness Report, Global Risks Report, Global Gender Gap Report.
